{{Quote|I am Bane Malar. I have many enemies, and must conceal my identity, so I apologize for the envirosuit.|Bane Malar|<ref name="dad">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Destroy All Droids promotional scenario}}</ref>}}
'''Bane Malar''' was a [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] in the employ of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He was hired to track down and apprehend inmates who escaped from the [[Spice mines of Kessel/Legends|Spice Mines of Kessel]]. Malar was quite good at his job, and soon enough mere mention of his name struck fear into the hearts of the inmates. While on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], Malar developed an addiction to [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]]. Though it enhanced his telepathic abilities, it also made him increasingly paranoid.

Malar also accepted jobs from other entities while on Kessel, such as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] and the [[Meatlumps]]. In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Black Sun hired him to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Jabba, and he accepted, making his way to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Once at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]], where he had an open invitation, he telepathically encountered the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. The encounter scared Malar, and he departed Tatooine, ruining the operation. In the hopes of staving off any trouble from Black Sun, he tried to liberate one of their agents from the Spice Mines but failed in the attempt, earning himself a [[Death mark/Legends|death mark]].

==Biography==
===Kessel operative===
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], Bane Malar was hired by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to monitor and track down escaping [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]] from the [[Spice mines of Kessel/Legends|Spice Mines of Kessel]]. He<ref name="db" /> rose to prominence as a result of his new employer.<ref name="SAV34">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|34|Star Wars A&ndash;Z}}</ref> Many political dissidents who had violated the Empire's ban on subversive music were likely among the prisoners.<ref name="Star Wars Blog">{{SW|url=news/slugthrowers-part-2|series=Slugthrowers: An Overview of Popular Music and Musicians in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:Kessel-EotECR.png|thumb|right|300px|Bane Malar hunted escapees from the Spice Mines of Kessel (Kessel pictured).]]
He armed himself with a powerful [[Noslo-19 slug rifle]] loaded with specialty ammunition from [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Arms]] and donned a [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Environment suit/Legends|enviro-suit]] that gave him an advantage in [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel's]] thin [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. In addition to his equipment, he was naturally [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]], giving him another advantage over his quarry. Malar took on the task of tracking escaped inmates across Kessel's surface and was able to return them. In [[Time/Legends|time]], he was greatly feared by those working in the [[Spice/Legends|Spice]] [[Mining/Legends|Mines]], and those he returned to confinement were terrified of him, swearing at every turn they could hear him whispering in their ears and compelling them to surrender.<ref name="db" />

Malar enhanced his abilities with [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]] spice from Kessel's mines. The spice allowed him to touch the minds of those he targeted, affecting them and making him an even more effective hunter. Malar became heavily addicted to the glitterstim to the point where he had to outfit his suit with inhalers, allowing him to enjoy regular doses of the spice. Although his skills continued to be above par, Malar became increasingly paranoid. He began to take contracts from other employers while on Kessel&mdash;if someone the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] wanted dead was working in the spice mines, Malar made sure they were killed while trying to escape.<ref name="db" /> To enhance his capacity to track down his quarry, Malar was known to pay fellow bounty hunter [[Tutti Snibit]] for his valued intel.<ref name="mag7">{{SW|url=news/the-not-so-magnificent-seven|text=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|int=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|nolive=1}}</ref>

===Corellia and Tatooine===
{{Quote|I can sense your questions, as I am able to read your mind.|Bane Malar|<ref name="dad" />}}
[[File:Malar_tk.jpg|thumb|left|280px|Bane Malar disarms an opponent with telekinesis.]]
At some point Malar was hired by the [[Meatlumps]] gang from [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] to take care of a group of rogue [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. Malar decided that he needed a partner for the job, so he contacted a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] and arranged a meeting with the individual at a local [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]]. There, he explained the situation to his temporary partner: a lone [[Mustafar panning droid|DLC-13 mining droid]] had gone rogue and reprogrammed a large number of other droids to serve his purposes. The only way to remove the droids from the Meatlumps' hideout was to destroy them all. After a few days of preparations, Malar and the spacer went down into the Meatlumps' hideout, where they were attacked by dozens of droids, as ordered by the lava collector. Malar fought like a man possessed, utilizing his slug rifle with great efficiency. In the close quarters of the Meatlump basement, the droids were furious adversaries. All of the droids, including the DLC-13, were eventually defeated.<ref name="dad" /> At another point, Malar came to confront a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]], on whom he employed [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]] as a disarming tactic.<ref name="swgtcg">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Bane Malar}}</ref>

Although he rarely left Kessel, Malar had an open invitation to the [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]],<ref name="db" /> one of the Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]],<ref name="rotj">{{Film|VI}}</ref> on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="db" /> which he occasionally visited. His appearances there sparked rumors about his telepathy and that he used his abilities to steal secrets.<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|pack=#07: Bane Malar|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLC07Bane.asp}}</ref> He was later offered a considerable sum by the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Jabba<ref name="db" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="date">{{DB|character|banemalar|Malar, Bane}} establishes that Bane Malar was in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] at the same [[Time/Legends|time]] as [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], an event that ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref> and, seeing it as a way to obtain more [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]] for spice, Malar accepted the task. Traveling to the Hutt's palace, the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter planned to kill Jabba by placing some tainted spice in the crime lord's [[Hookah pipe/Legends|hookah pipe]].<ref name="db" />

On arrival, Malar telepathically connected with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and was given reason to believe that Skywalker would somehow cause Malar's own [[Death/Legends|death]]. Panicking, the bounty hunter fled Tatooine and returned to Kessel. In order to placate Black Sun, he attempted to help one of their agents escape from Imperial custody but failed in the attempt. Left with no other choice, Malar departed from Kessel, the source of his glitterstim, only now with a [[Death mark/Legends|death mark]] on his head for the first time in his career.<ref name="db" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Can't read the droids. Won't know what they're planning.|Bane Malar|<ref name="dad" />}}
Despite proficiency in his craft, Malar became highly unstable when addicted to glitterstim, and it affected his ability to operate as a bounty hunter. Nevertheless, he was universally feared by prisoners due to his telepathic abilities. Malar's addiction evolved to such a stage that he was reluctant to leave Kessel, and his only loves became money and glitterstim.<ref name="db" /> While working for the Meatlumps on Corellia, Malar's paranoia was apparent&mdash;even in breathable atmosphere, Malar kept his enviro-suit on to shroud his identity, as he believed that there were many who wanted to kill him. When going up against rogue droids, Malar became overly worried that they would be hard to combat, as he had no way of reading their minds. He later fought like a man possessed against the droids occupying the Meatlump basement.<ref name="dad" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Control the mind, control the body.|Bane Malar|<ref name="dad" />}}
With his telepathic abilities, Malar invaded the minds of his quarry. His addiction to glitterstim only enhanced his capabilities.<ref name="db" /> When meeting with others, Malar could use his powers to divine their questions, allowing him to truncate conversations.<ref name="dad" /> Malar was also able to use telekinesis to disarm opponents<ref name="swgtcg" /> and was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]].<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Bane Malar}}</ref>

==Equipment==
In addition to his slug rifle, Malar was armed with a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. He wore a [[Helmet/Legends|helmet]] that completely covered his head as well as a black enviro-suit that was additionally topped with two [[Bandolier/Legends|bandoliers]].<ref name="Hasbro" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BaneMalarCCG-Card.png|thumb|right|265px|Bane Malar was brought into canon via a card in the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game.]]
Bane Malar was created for the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="insider158">{{InsiderCite|158|Star Wars Style Part 6: Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'' Style Part 6: ''Return of the Jedi''}}</ref> although he does not actually appear in the finished film.<ref name="rotj" /><ref name="Hasbro" /> Malar was first named in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity with the ''[[Jabba's Palace Limited]]'' set of [[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]],<ref name="ccg" /> though he was already introduced into the continuity when an image of the character had been revealed prior in the [[1992]] ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Bill Slavicsek]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="httes">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Malar was originally intended to appear in ''Return of the Jedi'' as a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Skiff/Legends|skiff]] guard,<ref name="insider158" /> but his backstory was changed when [[Edward M. Erdelac]], writing as "caledre," elaborated upon his past through [[StarWars.com]]'s [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]"<ref name="db" /> Malar was the last ''[[Star Wars]]'' element put up in the feature before it finished<ref name="jcf" /> on [[March 27]], [[2008]].<ref name="FansSetTheFacts"> {{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/news20080321.html|text=What's the Story: The Fans Set the Facts}}</ref> On the [[Jedi Council Forums]], Erdelac mentioned that he had intended to identify the character as a [[Draethos/Legends|Draethos]], but the reference was cut.<ref name="jcf">{{JCFCite|url=posts/28246880|board=Literature|thread=Official "What's the Story?" Hyperspace Databank Feature Discussion|user=Caledre|date=2008-03-27|time=9:21 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907225920/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/official-whats-the-story-hyperspace-databank-feature-discussion.20434695/page-97}}</ref>

Bane Malar's ''Return of the Jedi'' costume included a helmet that was created from a modified motorcycle helmet.<ref name="insider158" /> In 2009, Malar was included in the "Destroy All Droids" promotional scenario in the ''[[Galactic Hunters]]'' expansion of the [[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game|''Star Wars Galaxies'' Trading Card Game]]. That was therefore his first full appearance, in which the character exhibits traits outlined in Erdelac's [[Databank (original)|original Databank]] entry.<ref name="dad" />
